# midr <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138"/>

<!-- badges: start -->

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/ryo-asashi/midr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ryo-asashi/midr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml) [![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/midr)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=midr)

<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of 'midr' is to provide a model-agnostic method for interpreting and explaining black-box predictive models by creating a globally interpretable surrogate model. The package implements 'Maximum Interpretation Decomposition' (MID), a functional decomposition technique that finds an optimal additive approximation of the original model. This approximation is achieved by minimizing the squared error between the predictions of the black-box model and the surrogate model. The theoretical foundations of MID are described in Iwasawa & Matsumori (2026) [Forthcoming], and the package itself is detailed in [Asashiba et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08338).

## Installation

You can install the released version of **midr** from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/) with:

``` r
install.packages("midr")
```

and the development version from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ryo-asashi/midr")
```

## Surrogate Modeling and Component Plots

In this example, we fit a random forest to the `Boston` housing dataset (`ISLR2`) and construct a two-dimensional MID surrogate with `interpret()`.

```{r interpret}
library(midr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(ranger)
theme_set(theme_monograph())
midr_options(qualitative = "ukiyoe")
data("Boston", package = "ISLR2")
set.seed(42)
idx <- sample(nrow(Boston), nrow(Boston) * 0.75)
train <- Boston[ idx, ]
valid <- Boston[-idx, ]

fit_rf <- ranger(medv ~ ., train, mtry = 5)
mid <- interpret(medv ~ .^2, train, fit_rf, lambda = 0.1)
mid

preds_rf <- predict(fit_rf, valid)$predictions
preds_mid <- predict(mid, valid)
loss <- c(
  ranger_rmse = sqrt(mean((valid$medv - preds_rf)^2)),
  surrogate_rmse = sqrt(mean((preds_rf - preds_mid)^2))
)
loss
```

Component functions can be visualized using either base graphics (`plot()`) or `ggplot2` (`ggmid()`). Setting `main.effects = TRUE` (or `terms = "lstat * dis"`) displays the total of main and interaction effects.

```{r ggmid}
wrap_plots(
  ggmid(mid, "lstat") + labs(subtitle = "Main Effect: lstat"),
  ggmid(mid, "dis") + labs(subtitle = "Main Effect: dis"),
  ggmid(mid, "lstat:dis") + labs(subtitle = "Interaction: lstat:dis"),
  ggmid(mid, "lstat*dis", type = "compound") +
    labs(subtitle = "Total Effect: lstat*dis")
)
```

Perspective plots (`persp()`) are supported in **midr** starting from version 0.7.0.

```{r persp}
par_monograph(mar = rep(0, 4))
persp(mid, "lstat*dis", theta =135, theme = "steps")
```

## Post-Hoc Explanations

**midr** provides unified `eval_*()` functions for global importance, local prediction breakdowns, and individual conditional expectations (ICE; Goldstein et al., 2015).

### Term and Variable Importance

`eval_importance()` summarizes the contribution of each main and interaction term, or aggregates them by variable with `by = "variable"`.

```{r eval_importance, fig.asp = 0.45}
imp <- eval_importance(mid)
imp_var <- eval_importance(mid, by = "variable")

wrap_plots(
  nrow = 1L,
  ggmid(imp, max.nterms = 18, theme = "ukiyoe", legend = "bottomright") +
    labs(subtitle = "Term Importance"),
  ggmid(imp_var) +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(subtitle = "Variable Importance")
)
```

### Prediction Breakdowns

`eval_breakdown()` decomposes individual predictions into additive term effects. Passing multiple indices to `rows` returns a `midbrks` collection for side-by-side comparison.

```{r eval_breakdown, fig.asp = 0.45}
bds <- eval_breakdown(mid, data = valid, rows = c(1L, 9L))
labels(bds) <- c("Row1", "Row9")
wrap_plots(
  nrow = 1L,
  ggmid(bds[[1L]], legend = "bottomright") +
    labs(subtitle = "Waterfall Breakdown (Row 1)"),
  ggmid(bds, type = "dotchart", legend = "bottomleft") +
    labs(subtitle = "Comparison (Rows 1 vs. 9)")
)
```

### Conditional Expectations (ICE)

`eval_conditional()` computes ICE curves for the full model or for any submodel extracted with `subset()`.

```{r eval_conditional, fig.asp = 0.45}
ice_full <- eval_conditional(mid, "lstat", max.nsamples = 100L)
ice_int  <- eval_conditional(subset(mid, terms = "lstat:dis"), "lstat", max.nsamples = 100L)

wrap_plots(
  nrow = 1L,
  ggmid(ice_full, type = "centered") +
    labs(subtitle = "Centered ICE: lstat"),
  ggmid(ice_int, var.color = dis) +
    labs(subtitle = "Interaction Component: lstat:dis")
)
```

## Multi-Model Comparison and SurvMID(t)

Multiple MID models can be bundled with `midlist()` (producing a `mids` / `midrib` collection) to compare surrogates across different black-box models or hyperparameters.

```{r multi_model, fig.asp = 0.45}
lm_fit <- lm(medv ~ ., train)
mid_lm <- interpret(medv ~ ., train, lm_fit, k = 2)
mids <- midlist(
  "Random Forest" = mid,
  "Linear Model" = mid_lm
)

wrap_plots(
  nrow = 1L,
  ggmid(mids, "lstat", legend = "topright") +
    labs(subtitle = "Main Effect Comparison"),
  ggmid(
    eval_importance(mids),
    max.nterms = 14,
    legend = "bottomright"
  ) +
    labs(subtitle = "Importance Comparison")
)
```

When `interpret()` is given a prediction function that returns an $n \times K$ matrix—such as survival probabilities evaluated at multiple time horizons $t_1, \dots, t_K$—it automatically fits a time-dependent collection (**SurvMID(t)**) in a single call.

```{r survmid, fig.asp = 0.45}
library(survival)
data("veteran", package = "survival")

cox_fit <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ karno + age + celltype, data = veteran)

smid <- interpret(
  Surv(time, status) ~ karno + age + celltype,
  data = veteran,
  model = cox_fit,
  lambda = 0.1
)

wrap_plots(
  nrow = 1L,
  ggmid(smid, "karno + 1", type = "series", legend = "topright") +
    labs(subtitle = "SurvMID(t): Effect of karno"),
  ggmid(smid, "celltype + 1", type = "series", legend = "topright") +
    labs(subtitle = "SurvMID(t): Effect of celltype")
)
```

## References

[1] Iwasawa, H. & Matsumori, Y. (2026). "A Functional Decomposition Approach to Maximize the Interpretability of Black-Box Models". [Forthcoming]

[2] Asashiba, R., Kozuma, R. & Iwasawa, H. (2025). "midr: Learning from Black-Box Models by Maximum Interpretation Decomposition". <https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08338>

[3] Goldstein, A., Kapelner, A., Bleich, J., & Pitkin, E. (2015). "Peeking Inside the Black Box: Visualizing Statistical Learning With Plots of Individual Conditional Expectation". *Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics*, *24*(1), 44–65. <https://doi.org/10.1080/10618600.2014.907095>
